findings.source_passage: What happened in actual fact to a young man who ran incessantly and persistently through the London streets?
findings.source_locator: second paragraph, the novel-reading reflection on following someone
findings.why_it_matters: This rhetorical question is the comedic centrepiece of Christie's ironic digression on fictional versus real-world pursuit; the draft compresses the paragraph but deletes this voice-establishing line entirely, losing the satirical self-awareness that defines Tommy's character in this chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the rhetorical question verbatim within the compressed following-anxiety paragraph.

findings.source_passage: a taxi with flag erect turned the corner of the street ahead. Tommy held his breath. Would they hail it? He drew a sigh of relief
findings.why_it_matters: This miniature suspense beat dramatises Tommy's novice anxiety about the chase and is the payoff of the preceding comic digression; its complete absence flattens the tonal rhythm and erases a small but character-defining moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the taxi-passes-unchallenged beat in one compressed sentence to preserve the comedic suspense payoff.

findings.source_passage: the elderly chauffeur showed no interest. He merely grunted and jerked down his flag.
findings.source_locator: after 'Follow that other taxi—don't lose it'
findings.why_it_matters: This deadpan detail is tonally signature Christie: the cinematic movie-chase command met with complete British indifference. Dropping it loses a characteristic ironic beat and the contrast between Tommy's excitement and workaday London.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the chauffeur's grunt-and-flag reaction in a single brief clause.

findings.source_passage: He gave one doubtful look at them, then hurried into an adjacent telephone box. He dared not waste time in trying to get hold of Tuppence.
findings.source_locator: just before the phone call to Julius
findings.why_it_matters: The source gives Tommy's internal deliberation (which target to follow, why Tuppence is ruled out) as explicit reasoning; the draft collapses this to a single clause, losing the moment of tactical thought that shows Tommy's growing competence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clause restoring Tommy's conscious choice between following Boris versus Whittington.

findings.source_passage: Tommy fingered his pocket thoughtfully. In spite of the carte blanche assured to him, he had not yet acquired the habit of going about with any considerable sum of money
findings.source_locator: between booking the ticket and Julius's arrival
findings.why_it_matters: This brief self-deprecating aside characterises Tommy's chronic impecuniousness and sets up the Julius money-joke; without it, Julius's three-hundred-dollars line loses part of its comic contrast.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore in compressed form: a single sentence noting Tommy had only shillings left after buying the Bournemouth ticket.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium findings (taxi-anxiety beat, rhetorical pursuit question, chauffeur reaction) represent voice-flattening of Christie's comic irony but the critical Mr. Brown dialogue and the impersonation climax are well-preserved, keeping the draft above the regeneration threshold.
